subject: Request: One-time sustainment credit + term reset for TerraScope renewal
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: One-time sustainment credit + term reset for TerraScope renewal

Hi Lauren / Ben —

TerraScope (deal TS-2027-0427) is flagging for churn at renewal next month. They told me yesterday that several internal product teams are consolidating vendor spend and that the commercial terms need to move to a smaller committed seat count or they will not renew. This account is strategic in our analytics vertical and they are a reference for our GCP partnership.

Quick context: current ARR $420k, renewing at same tier would be $435k. Customer requests: reduce committed capacity by ~30% on renewal + 12-month term reset (start a fresh 12-mo from signing) and wants a one-time sustainment credit to offset migration costs. They are also asking for an SLA uplift (99.9% uptime credit language) for six months to cover their go-live window.

Ask: I recommend we offer a one-time $85,000 sustainment credit (applied to first invoice), a 12-month term reset (re-base their committed units to the lower level for the next term), and a temporary SLA addendum (99.9% uptime, with a 30% service credit cap for the first 6 months). The alternative is losing the account or a protracted procurement cycle.

Impact: approximate 1st-year revenue hit ~$85k + ~10% net ARR erosion due to lower commit. Finance indicates this is within a tolerable range if we classify as a one-time concession tied to an accelerated renewal signing (signed within 21 days).

Attachments: Q2 usage metrics (shows they were within expected patterns), the proposed adjusted renewal quote, and the procurement request they sent (procurement wants DocuSign cadence and PO terms).

Can we get an exec sign-off on the concession package (credit + term reset + SLA addendum)? Ben — will need your final ops confirmation on contract language and finance treatment. Marissa — pinging you for quick approval or alternatives.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time sustainment credit + term reset for TerraScope renewal

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I can greenlight:

- Can you confirm retention risk: are they 100% off the platform if we don't concede vs 50/50? (helps justify size of credit)
- Are there any outstanding reliability incidents or escalations we should factor into SLA language?
- Do we have a precedent for a term reset + credit combo in the past 12 months? If so, please point to the deal id.

Operationally I want to limit precedent exposure. If we do a credit, let's gate it to: (A) signed renewal within 21 days, (B) a 12-month minimum with a no-early-cancel clawback on the credit, and (C) an executive-approved exception to our standard SLA appendix for a 6-month pilot window only.

If Ben confirms contract language and Finance confirms the accounting, I can sign off on the package and route to Marissa for final exec approval.

-Lauren
VP, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time sustainment credit + term reset for TerraScope renewal

Lauren — answers inline and forwarding customer note below for context.

- Retention risk: Customer indicated they have a competing internal evaluation and will likely pause renewal if we do not provide some transition support — assessed by their buyer as ~75% chance to churn.
- Reliability incidents: No active Sev1s in the last 12 months; two Sev2s in Q1 tied to a spike in inference traffic (all resolved, RCA attached in the metrics PDF).
- Precedent: We did a similar combo for AuroraSoft (deal AU-2027-0119) but that included staged credits and a longer 18-month concession window. I believe the Aurora credit was $60k.

Customer original note (forwarded):

Our teams are evaluating consolidation options — the credit helps cover the engineering migration and the SLA addendum is critical for our launch. Without it, procurement is likely to push for an RFP.

Elena

Jonas

Also need Finance to confirm revenue recognition treatment and whether this should be recorded as contra-revenue or a one-time credit.

If we can get Ben's greenlight by EOD tomorrow, Lauren — can you route to Marissa for final authorization? Customer is ready to sign within the requested window.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Looping Finance (internal ops note) — I ran the numbers with FP&A. Recommendation below and operational changes required: 

- Approve one-time $85,000 sustainment credit (record as contra-revenue; Finance confirms the impact is a net ARR hit concentrated in year 1).
- Approve 12-month term reset with the following clawback: if customer terminates within 12 months, credit is recaptured pro rata.
- Approve 6-month SLA addendum (99.9% uptime) as a time-boxed appendix; legal to include explicit non-precedent language and automatic expiry.

Contract / Ops items: please include the clawback clause, route for DocuSign with the PO number, and set renewal to auto-renegotiate at the end of the new term without additional credit. 

Marissa — per Lauren's ask, this fits within tolerance for strategic retention. Recommend you sign the exec approval memo (one paragraph) and I'll attach FP&A impact note. If approved, I will prepare the DocuSign envelope and the amended SLA appendix.

-ben
